# ReflectionProbe

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("ReflectionProbe")`

Captures what a room looks like from one point, so that surfaces in the room reflect it and are lit by it instead of by the sky. Parent it to a part: the part's box is the area the probe applies to, and the walls its reflections are corrected against. Under anything other than a part it does nothing.

For a room, use an invisible part the size of the room, with `Transparency` at 1 and `CanCollide` and `CanQuery` off, and put the probe under it. A surface uses the probe whose box contains the point just in front of it, so the floor and walls of a room use that room's probe, and each side of a thin wall between two rooms reflects its own room.

The probe captures six images of every anchored object from its position. Inside the box, a shiny surface reflects the room and a matte surface is lit by it. Outside every probe's box, surfaces use the sky.

It is visual only: each machine captures its own, and nothing a script reads depends on it. No probes are captured when `GraphicsService.Reflections` is `Low`.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Blend` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The distance, in meters, over which the probe fades out beyond the faces of its box, where no other probe applies. Inside the box it applies fully. Two probes whose boxes meet blend across the boundary, so a doorway between two rooms shows no seam. |
| `BoxProjection` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether reflections are corrected for the walls of the box, so that a floor reflects a wall where the wall actually is. Turn it off for a probe outdoors, whose box is not a room. |
| `Dynamic` | `boolean` | — | read/write | Whether the probe is captured again when the lighting changes, such as when the sun moves or a light inside its box is switched on. It captures one image per frame. When it is off, the probe is captured once and again on `Refresh`. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the probe applies. A disabled probe does not count toward the number of probes a machine keeps, and surfaces in its box use the sky. |
| `Intensity` | `number` | `1` | read/write | A multiplier on the light the probe provides. |
| `Offset` | `vector` | `vector.zero` | read/write | The position the probe captures from, relative to the center of the box, in the box's own space and in meters. Move it when the center of the room is inside an obstacle such as a pillar. |
| `Priority` | `number` | `0` | read/write | Which probe applies where two boxes overlap: the one with the higher number. An integer. Give a small probe around a mirror a higher priority than the probe of the room it is in. |

## Methods

### `IsReady(): boolean`

Returns whether the probe's most recently requested capture is finished. It is false from `Refresh` until the new capture is done. It is true at once on a machine that keeps no probes, and for a probe beyond the number the machine keeps. To wait: `if not probe:IsReady() then probe.Completed:Wait() end`.

### `Refresh()`

Requests a new capture. Call it after the room changes: a wall falls, a door opens, a room is built. A probe captured while another is already in place sees that probe's light, so calling it twice adds a second bounce of light.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Completed()`

Fires when the probe's capture finishes on this machine, each time `IsReady` changes from false to true. Each machine fires it at its own time.
